Subject: Thanks — Perf SLO follow-up + next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we run a formal benchmark: 

Call recap / SLO targets you mentioned:
- 99th percentile generation latency <= 200 ms for responses up to ~512 tokens (interactive UI).
- Sustained throughput target: ~200 QPS for the main inference endpoint (batching allowed)
- Peak concurrency target: support 40 concurrent sessions with streaming (partial tokens) enabled
- Business requirement: <1% tail error rate (timeouts/5xx) under sustained load

Our asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm these targets and whether 512 tokens is the right max sequence for the interactive path?
2) Please share the prompt sets / eval prompt samples you want in the benchmark (we discussed a subset for accounting + reconciliation flows).
3) We'll share a proposed benchmark methodology doc and a lightweight eval harness (instructions + scripts). Can you confirm an internal point-of-contact for bench runs?

I've attached a draft benchmark plan and a sample prompt CSV to get started (see attachments). Dev will propose measurement definitions and the harness steps.

Proposed timeline: benchmark run during the week of July 27; preliminary results by Aug 3.

Thanks — feel free to reply with edits to the targets above.

Best,
Marissa

Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary — that's helpful and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- 512 tokens is our typical interactive upper bound for reconciliation UIs; for some audit exports we may go up to 1k tokens but that's a separate background job. For the UI path, 512 is correct.
- Regarding throughput: 200 QPS is our target for peak daytime volume, but we expect short spikes to 300 QPS for ~60s during batch imports. We care most about tail latency during spikes.
- Streaming is a hard requirement for the UI; partial token streaming with sub-200ms first-byte is desirable for perceived interactivity.

Contact for bench runs: Priya Rao (cc'd) is the engineering lead and will coordinate. She can provide the canonical prompt set (sanitized) and a small test dataset for content variability.

We can aim for the week of July 27 but would prefer July 29 for the live run (internal resource constraints).

Regards,

Subject: Proposed benchmark methodology + measurement defs

Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks for confirming. Attached is a concise methodology and measurement-definition doc — highlights below and what we'll need from EdgeFin to make the run reproducible: redwood-eval-harness-instructions.md (attached).

Methodology highlights:
- Workloads: we will run two profiles: (A) interactive streaming (512-token max) and (B) background batch (1k tokens, non-streaming) to reflect your split.
- Traffic generator: open-source harness (scripted JMeter-like load with deterministic seeds) that replays prompt sets with controlled think-times and concurrency.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 generation latency (end-to-end), time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for streaming, tokens/sec throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, KV-cache hit rates, and error rates (timeouts/5xx).
- Warmup: 10 minutes of steady traffic to prime caches; measurement windows are 10 minutes each and we will run three windows per profile.
- Batching/quantization: we'll run baseline (no quantization) and one quantized profile where applicable — we'll note model variant and kernel choices so runs are reproducible.
- Reproducibility: harness records seeds, model checkpoints, hardware topology, and environment variables. We will persist logs and the raw traces for post-run analysis.

What we need from EdgeFin:
1) Canonical prompt CSV (sanitized) — please include metadata column with "intent" and "expected token length".
2) A small representative dataset (100-500 items) for variance testing.
3) Confirmation of model variant you want tested (we'll propose a Redwood-verified open model if you don't have a preference).

I attached the harness instructions and a short checklist for you. If you want, we can run the harness from Redwood's Dedicated pool (isolated infra) or provide instructions to run it inside your VPC.

Attachment: redwood-eval-harness-instructions.md

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Priya / Alex —

A couple of quick reproducibility notes from our infra/measurements side: 

- Please include the random seed column in the prompt CSV; even small changes (whitespace) can change tokenization and affect p99. Our harness will normalize whitespace but having seeds makes exact replay possible.
- Measurement windows should include a cold-start run (1 window) in addition to the warmup windows — this shows worst-case behavior.
- For streaming TTFB we will instrument at the application boundary (first chunk delivered to the client) and also capture the model compute-first-byte to separate network vs model time.
- If you have a preferred metric for perceived interactivity (e.g., first-byte <= 200 ms for >= 90% of sessions), state that explicitly so we can include it in the pass/fail criteria.

I'll also prepare a short checklist for the run (env vars, kernel flags, model checksum). Dev — can you include the exact command-line we will run for the July 29 run and the S3/Drive location where logs will be uploaded?

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Applied ML — Redwood Inference
